record.context_brief: Rational points on strict CI models
record.original_question: Does every strict conditional independence model for discrete random variables have a Q-rational point? Here a strict conditional independence model is the intersection of the positive orthant with the constructible set of tables for which a specified collection of conditional independence statements Xi ⊥⊥ Xj | XK holds and all other such statements do not hold.

evidence.quote: The corresponding strict CI variety is the set of tables for which the given CI statements hold but all other CI statements do not hold.
The corresponding strict CI model is the intersection of the strict CI variety with the positive orthant.
Bonus Problem: Does every strict CI model have a Q-rational point?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X_1, \ldots, X_n$ be discrete random variables with $X_i$ taking values in a finite set of cardinality $d_i$. A joint distribution is represented by a nonnegative tensor $p = (p_{x_1,\ldots,x_n}) \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^{d_1 \times \cdots \times d_n}$ with $\sum p_{x_1,\ldots,x_n} = 1$. For disjoint subsets $i, j \in \{1,\ldots,n\}$ and $K \subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\} \setminus \{i,j\}$, the conditional independence (CI) statement $X_i \perp\!\!\!\perp X_j \mid X_K$ corresponds to a system of polynomial (quadratic) equations in the entries of $p$ (vanishing of certain $2\times 2$ minors of suitable flattenings).

Fix a collection $\mathcal{C}$ of CI statements among $\{X_1, \ldots, X_n\}$. The strict CI variety associated with $\mathcal{C}$ is the constructible subset of $\mathbb{R}^{d_1 \times \cdots \times d_n}$ consisting of all tensors $p$ such that every CI statement in $\mathcal{C}$ holds and every CI statement not in $\mathcal{C}$ fails. The strict CI model is the intersection of this constructible set with the strictly positive orthant (equivalently, the set of strictly positive probability tensors realizing exactly the CI statements in $\mathcal{C}$).

Question: Does every nonempty strict CI model (over all choices of $n$, dimensions $d_1, \ldots, d_n$, and collections $\mathcal{C}$) contain a point with all coordinates in $\mathbb{Q}$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as a "bonus problem" in a list of open problems in algebraic statistics. A web search did not reveal any subsequent paper resolving the existence of $\mathbb{Q}$-rational points on every strict CI model for discrete random variables; related literature on CI ideals, primary decompositions, and graphical model geometry does not address this specific rationality question. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Lectures on Algebraic Statistics
status_evidence.snippet: Algebraic structure of conditional independence models for discrete and Gaussian random variables, including CI ideals and their primary decompositions.
status_evidence.claim: Standard reference on algebraic CI models; does not address Q-rational points on strict CI models.

status_evidence.title: Algebraic Aspects of Conditional Independence and Graphical Models
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of algebraic approaches to conditional independence and graphical models.
status_evidence.claim: Survey covers structure of CI varieties but does not resolve the rational-point question for strict CI models.
